I'm posting to try to learn something. I don't understand why Google put resources into developing file-system level encryption when full disk encryption is the only way to truly protect user data. Why did Google invest in it?

Linux 4.1 kernel offers EXT4 file-system encryption
EXT4 file-system level encryption; is anyone else unimpressed? Everyone should be using Full Disk Encryption

First, it's not true that everyone should be using full disk encryption. Certain machines, e.g. cloud servers, like the ones Google probably manages, absolutely don't need it and shouldn't pay the performance hit for it.

Second, this is for different use cases that full-disk encryption is for. Certainly you wouldn't choose ext4 encryption over full-disk for your average laptop, etc. But it's easy to imagine a case where you'd want to choose which directories to encrypt (or not) in a dynamic way without necessary re-formatting everything. Perhaps, again, cloud servers, where various client files need to be encrypted in different ways and with different keys, but might just as quickly need to be deleted entirely, copied, moved, etc.

Or, maybe you don't have access to the full disk or partition, who knows. I'd say it's better to have the option there for those who need it, all else being equal.

This is a huge advancement for fine-grained encryption, and will be used heavily in niches where that's advantageous.

Perhaps the situation is different for cloud, but I haven't had anyone explain how exactly yet. I would be interested in hearing if EXT4 file-system encryption would provide more security than full-disk in protecting OPM data for example. Full-disk obviously needs the keys in memory whereas file-system only needs them in memory when decrypted. So perhaps this is an advantage? But then file-system encryption leaks so much metadata that that can often be leveraged in attacks of its own.

I mean if you really truly want to protect your data, you need deniable encryption. LUKS isn't enough (or too much rather) because there are headers at the beginning of the disk that say "HEY LOOK THERE'S ENCRYPTED DATA HERE". ( EDIT:The reason they exist is to tell what the encryption algorithm was and other related options. With plain dm-crypt youd have to specify thesr options every time the disk was mounted) Thus you're presented with the $5 wrench problem.

Deniable encryption would be either using plain dm-crypt with your /boot on a separate flash drive or LUKS with detatched headers (which could be on an additional flash drive or on the same one as /boot). That way your hard drive would look no different than if it had just been over written with random data. Having /boot on a separate flash drive also protects against evil made attacks.

BONUS: you could use a patched version of LUKS that allows you to set a Nuke passphrase so that if someone were to beat you to get the passphrase, you could give him that and it would wipe the LUKS headers thus making the data unrecoverable. He'd probably kill you but at least the data would be safe.

I began lifting when I was 13 to look good for the girls.. A bad choice I know. When I was 14 I made my high schools varsity weightlifting team and began lifting like a powerlifter and training my bench press. (High school competitions in Florida consist of one bench and one clean and jerk) . Then when I was 15 I began training for wrestling developing a tough, tight body that was powerful but I dislocated my elbow and quit wrestling. After battling depression (a lot was going on) I came back doing back squats with my arm in a sling. It wasn't easy. I craved to do full lifts again the entire time I was injured and watched so much weightlifting on youtube and began to study Olympic Weightlifting. When I was cleared to use my arm again I began practicing the clean and jerk (which I broke all the records for in Florida those can be seen on my youtube channel "Tom Piscopo") After becoming a state champion I earned the opportunity I had been dreaming of while watching all those Olympic lifters. I was being recruited to the Northern Michigan University Olympic Training Site. I quickly jumped on top of it and the coach began training me. Then the beginning of my senior year of highschool I was assaulted after school by what I thought to be my bestfriend. I lost some hearing in my left ear and had my thumb broken. To my dismay I had to travel to NMU (22 hours away) the day after surgery so I couldn't be put out with anesthesia. I did my best at the interview despite numbing pain and passing out a few times during the journey. After returning I really thought I had failed and lost out of the best opportunity of my life, but to my relief Coach Newgard didn't give up on me. Then, when things were starting to look up my luck found it's way back around my girlfriend I had been dating for a year began cheating on me. From a guy who had never taken an interest in a relationship I gave her everything and she took it all. Again, I fell back into depression, but this time I tried something new. Started listening to Billy Joel, CCR, and the blues while lifting and I let my body figure out if it would lift with it's rage or love, would I happily stick 320lb. clean and jerks or would I do doubles on back squat while tears rolled down my cheek...

That's when I realized what lifting is. It's an outlet and all we have to do is plug in and let the energy fill us.
